authority: CLAUDE.md §9.4: a decision that affects future interpretation is written to Tier 4, not held in agent memory. Applies §8.4 and §13.4 (the categorical Phase 8 block, which covers preparatory drafting and binds this record's author as much as the runner), §8.1 and §8.3 (the repository computes no lump-sum figure and invents none), §12.1 to §12.4 (reviewability and the four status categories), §13.3 (no invented project fact), §17.1.4 and §17.6.3 (gate evaluation and gate results belong to the scheduler and the gate evaluator) and §15 (explicit failure over fabricated completion). Not a constitutional amendment; §14.5 is not engaged.
decision: Three of the four criteria are closed. Phase 8 reached released under the operator's six dispatches, candidate version 1 is imported as a document snapshot, and the leakage guard ran clean over the package built around it. The blind report is the one box left open, and it is open because the pinned assessor has not run, not because anything is blocked: the candidate resolves complete against the RIA profile and every evidence pack builds with its anchors intact.

decisions.decision: No Part B is drafted on this branch, by the runner or by hand, and the ticket is reported blocked rather than delivered against a hand-written candidate.
decisions.reasoning: §13.4 prohibits any Phase 8 activity, including preparatory drafting, before the budget gate passes, and §8.4 states that the block is unconditional and instrument-independent. A hand-written Part B would be the same activity under another author, and importing it as candidate version 1 would put a document into Tier 4 that no gated phase produced. The gate exists to stop exactly this, so satisfying the ticket by routing around it would make the demo worthless as a test of the engine. §15 makes the declared failure the correct output.
decisions.recorded_in: This record; the validation report's criterion 2; tests/test_demo_candidate_blind_baseline.py TestThePhase8BlockIsRecorded and TestNoCandidateVersionExists.

decisions.decision: The ESR intake record is written now, before the document it concerns exists.
decisions.reasoning: The intake is not a Phase 8 substep. §13.4 enumerates drafting, assembly, evaluator review and revision; an out-of-band dev-graph record of what is known about an Evaluation Summary Report is none of them, and the blind lane is never a runtime gate. Writing it now fixes the document identity the eventual import must use, which turns a later mismatch into a test failure instead of a judgement call. The builder never reads the intake directory, so the demo snapshot id does not move. The cost is real and recorded: an intake record is immutable, so a Part B imported under another document id needs a new intake id.
decisions.recorded_in: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/intake/demo-biodiv-2027-part-b-v1.json; the validation report's the_esr_intake block; TestTheEsrIntakeRecord.

decisions.decision: Availability is not_applicable, not unavailable, and prior_submission is false.
decisions.reasoning: The demo is a demonstration, not a submission. not_applicable says no report exists; unavailable would say one exists and was not obtained, which would be an invented fact under §13.3. The module declares availability and never infers it, so the field had to be set: prior_submission false on its own stores unknown, and unknown would understate what is known here.

decisions.decision: submission_id carries the sentinel NOT_SUBMITTED, and the schema gap is recorded as F3 rather than patched.
decisions.reasoning: record_esr_intake requires a submission_id and offers no way to declare that no submission exists. A sentinel that reads as an absence cannot be mistaken for a submission number, so it does not invent a fact. Changing the schema to make the field optional is a Milestone 1 defect fix and touches a record type two lanes already read; doing it inside a demo ticket would widen the ticket into engine work the ticket did not ask for.
decisions.recorded_in: F3 in the validation report; TestTheEsrIntakeRecord.

decisions.decision: F1, the document-route anchor mismatch, is recorded unfixed with two candidate fix shapes and no choice between them.
decisions.reasoning: The fix changes either what a document snapshot is (sub-sections become part of the record) or what a profile declares (a passage-to-anchor map). Both are schema changes to shared artifacts, and the first changes the input the drafter writes. Picking one inside a demo ticket would let a ticket settle a design question for the engine, which is the §13.6 anti-pattern in miniature. The defect is reproduced by a test, so the fix has a failing case waiting for it.

decisions.decision: The defect is reproduced in a temporary graph root over the synthetic fixture, never by importing a document into docs/.
decisions.reasoning: A document record in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/documents/ would add an artifact_version node to the demo snapshot and move its snapshot id, which ticket 8 pinned at 116 nodes and 305 edges and which three records cite. A reproduction must not change the world it reports on. The synthetic fixture already carries the sources, objectives and participants the builder needs, so the copy is cheap.

decisions.decision: Criterion 4 is recorded as not met and its ticket box stays open, even though the guard ran clean over every blind package the demo world holds.
decisions.reasoning: assert_no_leakage ran over all 6 stored blind packages and they are clean, which is a real check on real records, though F6 shows those packages hold no passage, claim or commitment item and so cannot carry the leak. It is not the check the criterion asks for, which is the guard running over the package built around candidate version 1. Marking the box done would let a later reader believe the Part B package had been guarded. The distinction is between a check that ran and the check that was asked for, and §15 resolves it the same way as criteria 2 and 3.

decisions.decision: No gate_result.json is written for Phase 7 or Phase 8, and no runner phase is dispatched.
decisions.reasoning: §17.6.3 reserves gate result artifacts to the gate evaluator and §17.1.4 reserves gate evaluation to the scheduler. The gate's predicates are pure functions and may be read; their verdict may not be written as a gate result by anything else. Dispatching a phase is the operator's step on this repository.
decisions.recorded_in: This record; the validation report's the_gate block; the test module's header.

decisions.decision: Carry an 'assumed' claim as the 'unconfirmed' strength with an explicit 'Assumed' declaration, rather than widening the graph's evidence-strength vocabulary.
decisions.reasoning: The graph's four strengths describe how a claim is evidenced. Assumed describes a claim that is not evidenced at all and was declared by an operator instead, which is why EVIDENCE_TO_STATUS has no entry that yields it. The importer already models this: it admits one override, 'Assumed over Unresolved', mirroring the flip assumption_applier makes in Phase 8. Adding a fifth strength would let a lookup assert a declaration and would contradict section 12.2's distinction between Assumed and the evidenced categories.

decisions.decision: Scope a candidate's claim id to its section rather than dropping a declaration repeated across sections.
decisions.reasoning: A Tier 5 claim_id is a declaration key: all three Phase 8 sections assert project_duration, and each did so in its own ledger. A graph claim node belongs to one section with an id unique in the document, so the identity is the pair. The blind route files a claim into the ledger of its own section_id, so attributing a shared declaration to the first section would have thinned the other two. The join stays reversible: partition once on the separator and the Tier 5 id is the remainder.

decisions.decision: Collapse an exact repeat within one section, and refuse a repeat that disagrees.
decisions.reasoning: The section assembler concatenates the per-sub-section ledgers without deduplicating, so a declaration cited in four sub-sections arrives four times with an identical status and summary. The repeat carries nothing the first entry did not. A repeat that disagrees is a contradiction, and section 12.3 forbids resolving one by picking the more convenient side, so it fails closed instead.

decisions.decision: Import candidate version 1 into docs/ and accept that the demo snapshot id moves, rather than keeping the import in a temporary graph root.
decisions.reasoning: The criterion asks for a document snapshot with state imported, which is a durable Tier 4 record and not a test fixture. The 1 October report kept the import out of docs/ because there was no real Part B to import and moving the pinned snapshot id would have bought nothing. There is one now. The snapshot moved from 116 nodes to 267, and tools/build_demo_dev_graph.py rewrote the summary, the snapshot and the packages so the committed record describes the graph that exists.

decisions.decision: Leave the 36 superseded package directories on disk and record them, rather than pruning them.
decisions.reasoning: They belong to snapshots that no longer exist, so they cannot be rebuilt and a deletion is not reversible by re-running the builder. The cost of leaving them is that a count taken from the directory listing overstates the live package set, which is exactly the error the 1 October evidence made. Recording the count and deriving the live set from the builder's own summary fixes the reading without destroying the records.
decisions.recorded_in: F8, and the Milestone 2 candidates below

decisions.decision: Verify every input the blind report binds offline, and leave the assessor call to the operator.
decisions.reasoning: The assessor is an external model call. Running it to discover that an anchor is missing would spend the call on a question the pack builder answers for nothing. load_candidate, load_profile_bundle and build_pack_for were therefore run against the real candidate first: scope complete, six packs, anchors intact. What the run can still change is the grades, which are the assessor's to give.

decisions.decision: Reach the assessor over the Max subscription rather than hold an API key, and record what that costs.
decisions.reasoning: The operator declined to keep an API key for the demo. The harness refuses the claude_cli transport in two places, and both refusals govern the default-built backend only: Judge's own docstring names the injected backend as the seam for 'callers that wire their own transport' and makes transport independence the caller's responsibility there. harness/commands/_subscription_judge.py is that caller, and its module docstring discharges the responsibility by naming each axis. Model independence survives, because JudgeConfig still refuses every model in drafter_models() and so the assessor can never be the claude-opus-4-8 that drafted these sections. Context independence survives, and the blind lane rests on it: the transport is invoked with tools=None, so the assessor has no Read and no Glob and cannot open the drafting context, the assembled draft or the phase outputs. Transport independence does not survive. Vendor and family independence does not survive, and a same-family assessor is a weaker check on phrasing than a different-family one. The report records model@version and nothing else about the assessor, so the version tag is where the transport is declared, following the convention the Groq pin already used.

decisions.decision: Make the transport a flag rather than a replacement, and leave openai-compatible the default.
decisions.reasoning: The E5f rubric-grading track runs on the Groq pin and is paced for its free tier. Switching the default would have changed that lane silently. --transport selects; the independent path stays the default; the subscription path is the one the operator asks for by name.

decisions.decision: Override the assessor pin with flags rather than by editing .env.harness.
decisions.reasoning: load_harness_env loads the file with override=True, so an exported HARNESS_JUDGE_MODEL loses to the file and the operator cannot redirect one run from the shell. Editing the file instead would have unpinned the Groq lane that shares it. --assessor-model and --assessor-version win for one invocation and change no file; the file keeps its key and its own pin. The flags are a pin override and not a guard bypass: an overridden pin naming a drafter model is still refused.

decisions.decision: Lift the evidence-pack ceiling for the transport that has no rate limit, and for no other.
decisions.reasoning: See F9. The alternative offered was to decouple the cap from the provider on both transports; the operator chose the narrower change, so the Groq lane still cannot be handed a budget its TPM ceiling cannot carry, and a test pins that it still refuses one.

decisions.decision: Run the whole lane against a replaced transport before handing the command over.
decisions.reasoning: The same rule this ticket has followed throughout: the operator's calls must not be spent discovering something a free check would have found. The rehearsal is what surfaced F9, and it surfaced it by returning six cells that could not have passed.

decisions.decision: Close the ticket on the criterion as written, and record F12 against Milestone 2 rather than reopening it.
decisions.reasoning: Criterion 3 asks that the report carry the candidate hash, the profile version and the assessor pin, and be labelled complete or partial. It does so, on the header and on each of the six cells, and the label is 'complete'. The criterion does not ask the candidate to score well, and it must not: a blind pre-evaluation that only closes on a good grade is not a measurement. Four of six cells fail, and the systematic reason is F12, a defect in the route that builds the candidate rather than in the report that binds it. Holding the ticket open until the proposal grades better would confuse the lane working with the proposal being good.

decisions.decision: Verify the assessor's central claim against the artifacts before recording it as a finding.
decisions.reasoning: The assessor said in all six cells that every ledger entry carries an empty source_ref. An advisory judgment is not evidence, and 13.3 forbids recording a project fact that has not been read. So the 147 candidate claims were counted blank directly, the 180 Tier 5 entries were counted non-blank directly, and the two functions at the seam were read until the mechanism was explicit. The assessor was right, and F12 records the mechanism rather than the observation. This also fixes where the defect is not: the harness renders the field verbatim and is faithful, and the converter's choice to leave verified_span absent is correct and documented.

decisions.decision: Record the low implementation scores as not a defect, in the same register as the defects.
decisions.reasoning: F13. The demo's Tier 3 is almost entirely Assumed by construction, the sections concede it in the prose the assessor quotes back, and a blind assessor pricing that at roughly 0.3 is the lane working as specified. Left unrecorded next to F12, a reader of the report would take six scores and infer six defects. 12.2 distinguishes Assumed from Unresolved precisely so that a declared assumption is not read as a failure.

findings.summary: The dev-graph document route cannot feed either shipped instrument profile: one sub-section named for its section against rubric anchors B.1.1 to B.3.2 (RIA) and 1.1 to 3.2 (MSCA-PF).
findings.disposition: FIXED by ticket B on 2026-10-01. A document section carries an optional sub_sections list; the builder copies it onto the passage node and materialise_candidate emits it instead of synthesising one. The field is optional and an empty list normalises to absent, so no record's content_version moves. The anchor map still fails closed: a document declaring no sub-section, or declaring fewer than the profile anchors on, still raises. Proved by tests/harness/test_blind_document_subsections.py (22 tests).

findings.summary: An ESR intake can be stamped only through the document route, so F1 also blocks the demo's not_applicable availability from reaching any RIA blind report.
findings.disposition: FIXED with F1 by ticket B. An ESR intake now stamps onto a report produced through the document route, and demo-biodiv-2027-part-b-v1 is the record it was proved with.

findings.summary: record_esr_intake requires a submission_id with no way to declare that no submission exists.
Phase 8 has produced nothing. The gate is working; the outstanding step is the operator's planner run.
The demo world's 6 blind packages hold 0 passage, 0 claim and 0 commitment items, so they cannot carry the leak the guard looks for. The clean pass is correct and uninformative.
findings.disposition: recorded; it is why criterion 4's box stays open

findings.summary: The demo's 6 blind packages are all incomplete at budget 3000, and build_blind_evidence refuses an incomplete package.
findings.disposition: recorded; no change made, because no real package is built yet

findings.finding: The candidate builder had no mapping for an 'assumed' claim, so it refused the real Part B outright. CLAUDE.md section 12.2 defines four status categories and the builder's EVIDENCE_STRENGTH_BY_STATUS covered three. The omission is not an oversight in the lookup: the graph has no evidence_strength that yields Assumed, because Assumed is declared rather than evidenced. normalise_candidate admits exactly one override for this — 'only Assumed over Unresolved may be declared' — mirroring the flip assumption_applier makes. Carrying an assumed claim on strength alone would have landed it as Unresolved and silently discarded the operator declaration. The demo's Part B carries 85 such claims out of 180.
findings.disposition: FIXED. The builder maps 'assumed' to the 'unconfirmed' strength and declares 'Assumed' alongside it, through DECLARED_STATUS_BY_STATUS. Every other status is still derived by the graph. The declaration survives into the blind assessor's ledger: 11, 17 and 24 assumed claims reach the three materialised sections.

findings.finding: Two counting defects, found by converting a real Part B. First, a Tier 5 claim_id is a declaration key, not an occurrence id. All three sections assert project_duration, and the section assembler concatenates the per-sub-section ledgers without deduplicating, so one declaration arrives up to six times in one section with an identical status and summary. 180 ledger entries carry 122 distinct ids. A graph claim node belongs to one section and its id is unique across the document, so the identity is the pair. Second, the demo dev-graph builder never prunes: a snapshot shift leaves the previous generation's package directories on disk, so 54 directories now hold 18 current packages. The 1 October evidence for criterion 4 counted 36 directories and 6 blind packages, of which 18 and 3 belonged to a superseded snapshot.
findings.disposition: The first half is FIXED: the builder scopes each claim id to its section, collapses an exact repeat, and refuses a repeat that disagrees rather than picking a side (section 12.3). 180 entries become 147 claims. The second half is recorded unfixed and offered as a Milestone 2 candidate: pruning a superseded generation deletes records that cannot be rebuilt, which is the operator's call and not this act's.

findings.finding: One provider's free-tier rate limit was deciding how much of the Part B the assessor is allowed to read. MAX_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET was defined as GROQ_TPM_LIMIT - DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS - RUBRIC_PROMPT_ALLOWANCE = 6000 - 2048 - 900 = 3052, and build_evidence_pack refused any larger budget outright. Measured over the six candidate packs at the shipped default of 3000, that cap drops 111 of 266 relevant items and truncates every single cell; the implementation workplan cell loses 32 of its 53. The rubric system prompt then tells the assessor that a pack marked insufficient_context means 'you must not return passed: true'. Every grade in the report was therefore predetermined before any model read anything, and the report would have measured the rate limit rather than the proposal. The number is a property of the assessor's transport, not of the proposal or of the harness.
findings.disposition: FIXED. The ceiling is now a parameter, max_token_budget, threaded through build_evidence_pack, build_pack_for, grade_expectation and assess_candidate. It still defaults to MAX_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET, so every existing caller and the whole Groq lane are byte-for-byte unchanged; a transport with no per-minute token ceiling passes None, and then the operator's --budget alone governs. Lifting the ceiling does not lift the floor: a budget that is still too small reports insufficient_context exactly as before, and is never silently stretched to make a pack fit. The smallest budget at which all six candidate packs complete is 10501, bisected rather than estimated; UNCAPPED_DEFAULT_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET is 32768, a chosen constant whose basis is that measurement plus roughly threefold headroom.

findings.finding: A rejected API key printed a traceback instead of failing closed. blind_assessment's main converts a closed set of errors to exit code 2 with one readable line, and no transport error was in that set, so the 401 propagated out of assess_candidate through runpy and the operator read a twelve-frame stack trace for a configuration problem. The module docstring describes the command as fail-closed throughout.
findings.disposition: FIXED. A transport failure on either transport now prints one line and returns exit 2, like every other fail-closed condition. The check is lazy, so importing the command still pulls in neither transport, and it re-raises anything that is not a transport error rather than swallowing it. SubscriptionJudgeError was additionally made a JudgeError so a mismatched assessor pin lands in the same path.

findings.finding: Three real-data probes in tests/harness/test_evidence_pack.py (TestRealSections) fail on this branch, and they failed before this act. They read docs/tier5_deliverables/proposal_sections/ with the harness default rubrics, whose anchors are the MSCA-PF spelling '1.1', while Phase 8 wrote RIA sections declaring 'B.1.1' and 'B.1.2'. The anchor map fails closed, which is correct behaviour meeting a probe that hardcodes one instrument's spelling. The same mismatch is the F1 that ticket B fixed for the document route; the direct-section route still carries it in its test fixtures.
findings.disposition: OPEN, and out of this ticket's scope. A Milestone 2 candidate: the probe should resolve its anchors from the profile that matches the sections on disk, rather than assuming MSCA-PF. Recorded here so the three failures are not read as a regression from this act.

findings.finding: Every claim reaches the assessor with no source. All 147 claims in the candidate carry source_ref '', including the 90 declared 'confirmed', and the assessor named this in all six cells unprompted: 'every ledger entry carries an empty source_ref'. Upstream the field is intact. The three Tier 5 sections hold 180 claim_statuses entries and not one is blank; excellence_section's first is docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json. The break is a seam between two components that are each correct alone. tools/build_part_b_candidate.py::_claims maps claim_id, status and claim_summary onto the graph's claim shape and does not carry source_ref; its docstring explains, correctly, that it leaves verified_span absent because inventing offsets would defeat the claim verifier. harness/blind_assessment.py::materialise_candidate then derives source_ref from verified_span['id'] alone, which is the one field the converter deliberately never writes, so it resolves to ''. The harness is faithful throughout: evidence_pack renders the field verbatim as 'source_ref=' and the assessor judged what it was shown. Under CLAUDE.md 12.2 a 'confirmed' claim is one directly evidenced by a named source in Tier 1-3; in the candidate the name is gone, so the candidate understates its own traceability against a Tier 5 state that has it.
findings.disposition: OPEN, and out of this ticket's scope. The criterion asks what the report binds and how it is labelled, and the report binds and labels correctly. A Milestone 2 candidate, and the first finding on this branch produced by the blind assessor rather than by a deterministic check: no gate caught it, because every component passed its own contract. The fix is to carry the Tier 5 source_ref through the converter into the graph claim, and to have materialise_candidate prefer it over the absent verified_span rather than fall back to ''. Until then, every grounding judgment in a blind report on this route is made against a blank field and understates the candidate.

findings.finding: The two implementation cells score lowest, at 0.323 and 0.283, and the assessor's reasoning is that the load-bearing figures are not grounded: every person-month in Tables 3.1a and 3.1f reads 'not agreed' or 'TBD', the resources are deferred to a future lump-sum response, the risk register is flagged assumed, and all twelve partner_participation entries are assumed. That is not a defect in the draft. It is the demo's Tier 3 being almost entirely Assumed by construction, which ticket 4 recorded and 13.8 required the sections to concede, and the sections do concede it, in the prose the assessor quotes back: 'Every partner's participation is an operator assumption'.
findings.disposition: NOT A DEFECT, recorded so the scores are not read as one. The blind assessor priced an all-Assumed Tier 3 at roughly 0.3 on implementation and the drafts told it so plainly, which is the lane working. A real project would close these by confirming the consortium and receiving the budget; the fictional one cannot and must not.

milestone_2_candidates: Fix F1: decide where a section's sub-section structure lives, then make the document route feed a shipped profile. The failing case exists.
Fix F3: let an intake declare that no submission exists.

Re-run this ticket after the operator dispatches Phase 7 and Phase 8 reaches released. Criteria 2 and 3 are the only ones outstanding, and every Phase 8 figure will trace to the fictional budget, which §13.8 requires the deliverable to say.

Deduplicate the section assembler's claim ledger. It concatenates the per-sub-section ledgers, so one declaration lands up to six times in a section with an identical status and summary. The candidate builder collapses them, which fixes the reader and not the artifact.

Prune or index superseded dev-graph package directories. tools/build_demo_dev_graph.py writes content-addressed packages and never removes the previous generation, so 54 directories now hold 18 current packages and a directory count overstates the live set.
Resolve the real-section probes' anchors from the profile that matches the sections on disk instead of hardcoding the MSCA-PF spelling (F11).
Give the blind report a first-class assessor transport field, so the transport is structured data rather than a convention inside the version tag.

Carry the Tier 5 source_ref through tools/build_part_b_candidate.py into the graph claim, and have materialise_candidate prefer it over the absent verified_span instead of falling back to the empty string (F12). Until then every grounding judgment in a blind report on this route is made against a blank field.
